situation.en: It's evening in New York. You take a yellow cab from Penn Station to your hotel near Central Park. You need to give the address, ask roughly how long it will take and how much it will cost, and sort out a small problem with paying.
situation.he: ערב בניו יורק. אתם לוקחים מונית צהובה מפן סטיישן למלון ליד סנטרל פארק. צריך למסור כתובת, לשאול בערך כמה זמן זה ייקח וכמה זה יעלה, ולפתור בעיה קטנה בתשלום.

goal.en: Give your destination clearly, ask about the route, time and fare, and solve a payment or drop-off problem politely.
goal.he: למסור את היעד בבירור, לשאול על המסלול, הזמן והמחיר, ולפתור בנימוס בעיה בתשלום או בנקודת ההורדה.

phrases.en: Hi, could you take me to the Park View Hotel on West 58th Street, please?
phrases.he: היי, למלון פארק ויו ברחוב 58 מערב, בבקשה.

phrases.en: How long will it take with this traffic?
phrases.he: כמה זמן זה ייקח עם הפקקים האלה?

phrases.en: Roughly how much will it be?
Hi, is this the Uber for Dana?
phrases.note: With rideshares, check the driver's name, the car and the plate number before you get in.

phrases.en: Could you turn the AC down a little?
Could you drop me off at the corner, please?
Sorry, the card machine doesn't seem to be working.
phrases.he: סליחה, נראה שמכשיר האשראי לא עובד.

phrases.en: Do you take cash? I've only got a fifty.
phrases.he: אפשר לשלם במזומן? יש לי רק שטר של חמישים.
phrases.note: Mention a large bill (UK: note) early, so the driver can check they have change.

phrases.en: Could I get a receipt, please?

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Hi, could you take me to the Park View Hotel on West 58th Street, please?

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Between Sixth and Seventh, I think. How long will it take?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: With this traffic? Maybe twenty-five minutes.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: OK. And roughly how much will it be?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: It's on the meter, but probably around thirty bucks, plus tip.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Great, thanks... Oh, just here on the right is fine.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Sorry, the card machine back here doesn't seem to be working.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Ah, it does that sometimes. Give me a second... OK, try it now.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: That worked. Could I get a receipt, please?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Sure, it'll come up on the screen. Enjoy your stay!

options.text: Park View Hotel. It's somewhere near Central Park, I think.

feedback.en: It works, since drivers hear hotel names a lot, but 'somewhere near Central Park' is vague. The street name is more useful, and 'please' sounds friendlier.
feedback.he: זה עובד, כי נהגים שומעים שמות של מלונות הרבה, אבל somewhere near Central Park מעורפל. שם הרחוב שימושי יותר, ו-please נשמע ידידותי יותר.

options.text: Hi, the Park View Hotel on West 58th Street, please.

feedback.en: Short and polite, and the street name helps the driver find it quickly. In a taxi, the destination plus 'please' is all you need.
feedback.he: קצר ומנומס, ושם הרחוב עוזר לנהג למצוא את המקום מהר. במונית מספיק לומר את היעד ולהוסיף please.

options.text: I want to arrive to the Park View Hotel. Do you know where it is?

feedback.en: 'Arrive to' is wrong (it's 'arrive at'), and 'I want to arrive' sounds unnatural here. Rather than asking if the driver knows it, give the street: 'The Park View Hotel on West 58th Street, please.'
feedback.he: arrive to שגוי (אומרים arrive at), ו-I want to arrive לא טבעי כאן. במקום לשאול אם הנהג מכיר את המקום, אומרים את הרחוב: The Park View Hotel on West 58th Street, please.

model_replies: Hi, the Park View Hotel on West 58th Street, please.
Could you take me to the Park View Hotel? It's on West 58th Street.

practice.partner: I can take the highway or go straight up through Midtown. The highway's longer, but there's less traffic. Your call.

options.text: Take the short way, and don't try to cheat me.

feedback.en: Accusing the driver of cheating is rude and may start an argument. If you're worried about the fare, just ask: 'Roughly how much will it be?'
feedback.he: להאשים את הנהג ברמאות זה גס ועלול להוביל לוויכוח. אם המחיר מדאיג אתכם, פשוט שואלים: Roughly how much will it be?

feedback.en: Acceptable, but it can sound a bit careless. 'Whichever's quicker is fine' gives the driver a clear instruction.
feedback.he: סביר, אבל עלול להישמע אדיש. Whichever's quicker is fine נותן לנהג הנחיה ברורה.

options.text: Whichever's quicker is fine. Roughly how much will it be?

feedback.en: Lets the driver choose but gives a clear priority, and checks the fare. 'Your call' means 'you decide'.
feedback.he: נותן לנהג לבחור אבל עם עדיפות ברורה, ובודק את המחיר. Your call פירושו 'ההחלטה שלך'.

model_replies: Whichever's quicker is fine. Roughly how much will it be?
Let's take the highway if it's faster. About how much will that be?

practice.partner: Sorry, I can't stop right outside the hotel. There's construction. Is the corner OK?

options.text: Sure, the corner's fine. Thanks for letting me know.

feedback.en: Flexible and polite: you accept the change and thank the driver.
feedback.he: גמיש ומנומס: מקבלים את השינוי ומודים לנהג.

options.text: No, you must stop in front of the hotel. My bags are heavy.

feedback.en: 'You must' sounds like an order, and the driver may not be allowed to stop there. If your bags are heavy, ask politely: 'Could you get any closer?'
feedback.he: You must נשמע כמו פקודה, ויכול להיות שלנהג אסור לעצור שם. אם התיקים כבדים, שואלים בנימוס: Could you get any closer?

options.text: Yes, this is acceptable for me. I can walk from the corner to the hotel.

feedback.en: Understandable, but 'acceptable for me' is far too formal for a taxi, and you don't need to explain that you can walk. Say 'Sure, the corner's fine.'
feedback.he: מובן, אבל acceptable for me רשמי מדי למונית, ואין צורך להסביר שאתם יכולים ללכת ברגל. אומרים: Sure, the corner's fine.

model_replies: Sure, the corner's fine. Thanks for letting me know.
No problem, the corner works. Thanks.

practice.partner: Here we are. That's twenty-eight fifty. Just tap your card on the screen back there.

feedback.en: Clear, but it sounds like blame. 'The card machine doesn't seem to be working' is softer.
feedback.he: ברור, אבל נשמע מאשים. The card machine doesn't seem to be working רך יותר.

options.text: Sorry, the card machine doesn't seem to be working. Could you check it?

feedback.en: 'Doesn't seem to be working' describes the problem politely without blaming anyone, and you ask for help.
feedback.he: doesn't seem to be working מתאר את הבעיה בנימוס בלי להאשים אף אחד, ומבקש עזרה.

options.text: The machine is broken, so I don't pay. It's not my fault, it's your machine.

feedback.en: You still need to pay, and blaming the driver won't help. Explain the problem and suggest another way: 'Could I pay in cash, or could you restart the machine?'
feedback.he: עדיין צריך לשלם, ולהאשים את הנהג לא יעזור. מסבירים את הבעיה ומציעים דרך אחרת: Could I pay in cash, or could you restart the machine?

model_replies: Sorry, the card machine doesn't seem to be working. Could you check it?
Sorry, my card isn't going through. Could you restart the machine?

practice.partner: Sorry about that. It's still not working. Can you pay cash?

options.text: I have no cash. It's your problem.

feedback.en: Rude, and it doesn't solve anything. Suggest a solution: 'I don't have enough cash. Is there an ATM nearby?'
feedback.he: גס, ולא פותר כלום. מציעים פתרון: I don't have enough cash. Is there an ATM nearby?

feedback.en: It works, but it sounds abrupt. 'Sure, here you go' is friendlier.
feedback.he: זה עובד, אבל נשמע חד. Sure, here you go ידידותי יותר.

options.text: Sure, here's thirty-five. Keep the change.

feedback.en: Natural: rounding up and saying 'Keep the change' is a simple way to tip in a US taxi. Here that's a tip of just over 20%.
feedback.he: טבעי: לעגל כלפי מעלה ולומר Keep the change היא דרך פשוטה להשאיר טיפ במונית בארצות הברית. כאן זה טיפ של קצת יותר מ-20%.

model_replies: Sure, here's thirty-five. Keep the change.
No problem, here you go. Keep the change.

roleplay.persona: Luis, a talkative New York taxi driver who has been driving for twenty years. He's friendly, proud of knowing every shortcut, talks quickly and likes chatting about the city and baseball.
roleplay.complication: Luis suggests a longer route that he says is 'faster at this time of day', and at the end the card reader in the back stops working, so the learner has to ask about other ways to pay.

culture.en: In New York, yellow cabs charge by the meter, and passengers usually add a tip, often around 15-20%. With rideshare apps the price is usually shown before you ride, and you can tip in the app.
culture.he: בניו יורק המוניות הצהובות גובות לפי מונה, ונוסעים בדרך כלל מוסיפים טיפ, לרוב בסביבות 15-20%. באפליקציות הסעות המחיר מוצג בדרך כלל מראש, ואפשר להוסיף טיפ באפליקציה.

culture.en: In London, you can stop a black cab in the street and it uses a meter, while a minicab has to be booked in advance. People often round up the fare instead of tipping a set percentage.
culture.he: בלונדון אפשר לעצור ברחוב מונית שחורה, והיא נוסעת לפי מונה, ואילו מיניקאב צריך להזמין מראש. נוהגים לעגל את הסכום כלפי מעלה במקום לתת טיפ באחוזים קבועים.

culture.en: Before getting into a rideshare, check the driver's name, the car and the plate number in the app. If they don't match, don't get in.
culture.he: לפני שנכנסים לרכב של אפליקציית הסעות, בודקים באפליקציה את שם הנהג, הרכב ומספר הרישוי. אם משהו לא תואם, לא נכנסים.

variants.note: A UK motorway is a major multi-lane road, like a US freeway or interstate.
'Taxi' is understood everywhere; 'cab' is more common in the US, and a London taxi is a 'black cab'.
